newsitem.title: USA: Brady bonds end mostly higher in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Brady bonds end mostly higher in quiet trade.

text.p: Brady bond prices ended the New York session mostly higher on Monday, after what traders deemed a very quiet day with thin trading activity.
"Spreads tightened a little bit and bonds were better bid but trading has been fairly thin today," said one Brady trader.
Venezulan PARS were up 5/8 at 75-1/4 bid, DCBs were up 1/2 at 88 bid. Brazilian "C" bonds were up 3/8 at 79 bid and Mexico PARS were quoted up 1/4 at 74-3/4 bid.
"Bonds were better bid today...it looks like some dealers are using this opportunity to work off some inventory," another trader said.
Meanwhile, Argentine PARS and FRBs traded an 1/8 weaker at 66-1/8 bid, 90-3/8 bid, respectively.
"The market's tried to rally pretty strong today but there really wasn't strong support from the U.S. market," said Walter Molano, Director of Latam Economic Research at SBC Warburg.
Molano said uncertainty in the market surrounding the U.S. Federal Reserve Board's next interest rate move has kept players nervous and prices under pressure.

"We're going to get a better signal of that on Thursday and Friday when we get more key (U.S.) econmic data coming in," Molano said. "It could very well be that we get more data pointing towards a tightening by the Fed."

As the possibility of a Fed hike in interest rates looms over the market players will keep a watchful eye on Thursday's release of U.S. February retail sales figures followed by Friday's release of February producer prices.

In a Reuter poll, U.S. economists predict a 0.6 percent increase in February retail sales, unchanged from January's level. February Producer prices are expected to show a slight 0.1 percent decline versus a drop of 0.3 percent in January.
Elsewhere, Bulgarian IABs fell 3/4 to 60-7/8 bid while Russian VN US$ ended the trading day up 1/8 at 82-1/8 bid.
In the governmnet market, the benchmark U.S. 30-year Treasury bond closed off 1/32 at 97-17/32 to yield 6.82 percent.
